title: Direct Knowledge Of Allah 19th Degree 1st Truth From Searching In Absentia To Direct Address

questions.question: Who was learning a lesson of faith from the universe?
questions.answer: A traveler who really wanted to find the Creator.

questions.question: How many stages had the traveler gone through before this point?
questions.answer: Eighteen stages.

questions.question: What was the traveler looking for?
questions.answer: The Creator of the world.

questions.question: Where did the traveler come close to at the end of his climb in belief?
questions.answer: A place of truth near Allah’s presence.

questions.question: Who did the traveler speak to first?
questions.answer: His own soul.

questions.question: In the opening surah of the Qur’an, what kind of speech comes before the word “iyyaka”?
questions.answer: Praise spoken indirectly.

questions.question: What does the word “iyyaka” show in the passage?
questions.answer: Coming near and speaking directly to Allah.

questions.question: What does the traveler say people should leave behind?
questions.answer: Indirect searching.

questions.question: From whom should a person ask about the One he is seeking?
questions.answer: From the One he is seeking.

questions.question: What example is given to help explain this idea?
questions.answer: Asking the sun about the sun.

questions.question: Why is the sun used as an example?
questions.answer: Because the sun shows other things and can also show itself clearly.

questions.question: How can people try to know their Creator?
questions.answer: By learning about His Beautiful Names and His holy attributes.

questions.question: Do people know Allah fully or according to their ability in this passage?
questions.answer: According to their ability.

questions.question: What big idea does the passage teach about Allah?
questions.answer: Allah is the only true God.

questions.question: How is everything other than Allah described?
questions.answer: As created and needing Him.

questions.question: What does the passage say about anyone being like Allah?
questions.answer: No one can be like Him.

questions.question: What things in the universe are said to point to Allah?
questions.answer: The whole cosmos and all its parts.

questions.question: What are some pictures used for the cosmos in the passage?
questions.answer: A big book, a palace, and a city.

questions.question: What small and large parts of the cosmos work together in the description?
questions.answer: Its sections, pieces, and tiny parts.

questions.question: What does the passage say about things entering and leaving the world?
questions.answer: They are part of the signs that point to Allah.

questions.question: What truths about the world are mentioned as signs?
questions.answer: That it was made, that it changes, and that it depends on Allah.

questions.question: Whose agreement is mentioned in support of this truth?
questions.answer: The scholars of theology.

questions.question: What does the changing form of the world show when it happens with order and wisdom?
questions.answer: It shows signs of Allah’s wisdom and control.

questions.question: What kinds of teamwork are seen among beings?
questions.answer: Helping each other, answering each other’s needs, and supporting each other.

questions.question: What two other qualities are seen among beings besides teamwork?
questions.answer: Balance and protection.

questions.question: What do all these signs together point to?
questions.answer: Allah’s existence and oneness.

questions.question: What kind of traveler is described in the passage?
questions.answer: A very eager and curious traveler.

questions.question: What had the traveler gained through the eighteen stages?
questions.answer: Indirect knowledge of Allah.

questions.question: After learning indirectly, what new way did he reach?
questions.answer: Speaking directly in Allah’s presence.

questions.question: What word in the opening surah marks this change?
questions.answer: “Iyyaka.”

questions.question: What change happens at that word?
questions.answer: The speech changes from talking about Allah to speaking to Him.

questions.question: What comes before that word in the surah, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Words of praise.

questions.question: Why does the traveler say indirect seeking should be left?
questions.answer: Because he wants to ask directly from the One he seeks.

questions.question: What simple example is used to make this clear?
questions.answer: Learning about the sun from the sun.

questions.question: What can the sun do besides lighting other things?
questions.answer: It can make itself known too.

questions.question: What helps people know the sun in the example?
questions.answer: Its rays.

questions.question: What is compared to the sun’s rays in learning about Allah?
questions.answer: Allah’s Beautiful Names and sacred attributes.

questions.question: Does the passage teach that people can know Allah without any limit?
questions.answer: No, only as much as they are able.

questions.question: What does this teach a believer to do?
questions.answer: To turn to Allah and know Him through His names and qualities.

questions.question: What does the passage say first in a short summary of faith?
questions.answer: That Allah alone is God.

questions.question: What does “Necessary Existent” mean here in a simple way?
questions.answer: Allah truly exists and does not depend on anything.

questions.question: How are all other things different from Allah?
questions.answer: They are dependent and created.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah being one?
questions.answer: He is one and unique.

questions.question: What giant sign points to this truth?
questions.answer: The whole universe.

questions.question: What are three ways the universe is described to help us imagine it?
questions.answer: Like a book, a palace, and a city.

questions.question: Which parts of the universe are mentioned as agreeing in this testimony?
questions.answer: Its main parts, kinds, pieces, and tiny bits.

questions.question: What do the world’s changes help show?
questions.answer: That it is made by Allah and always under His control.

questions.question: What is said about the renewing of the world’s “letters and words”?
questions.answer: It happens with order and balance.

questions.question: What kind of relationships among living things are noticed clearly?
questions.answer: Cooperation, care, support, and answering needs.

questions.question: What else is seen among all beings besides care and support?
questions.answer: Balance and preservation.

questions.question: After all this learning, what did the traveler do?
questions.answer: He spoke to his own soul.

questions.question: In this passage, what does the traveler learn from the cosmos?
questions.answer: A lesson of faith about Allah.

questions.question: How far had he progressed in this learning journey?
questions.answer: He had gone through eighteen levels.

questions.question: What made the traveler keep searching?
questions.answer: His strong desire to find the Creator.

questions.question: At the end of his rise in belief, what special closeness is described?
questions.answer: Nearness to a place of truth in Allah’s presence.

questions.question: What did he say about the first part of the opening surah?
questions.answer: It is praise said in an indirect way.

questions.question: What does the word “iyyaka” help begin?
questions.answer: Direct speaking to Allah.

questions.question: What should replace indirect searching?
questions.answer: Asking Allah directly.

questions.question: Who should be asked for the one being searched for?
questions.answer: The very one being searched for.

questions.question: What object in the sky is used as an example?
questions.answer: The sun.

questions.question: What lesson does the sun example teach?
questions.answer: The one that lights other things can also show itself.

questions.question: What is one way people can know their Creator?
questions.answer: By His Beautiful Names.

questions.question: What is another way named in the passage?
questions.answer: By His sacred attributes.

questions.question: How much can people know in this way?
questions.answer: As much as their ability allows.

questions.question: What is the main person in this passage called?
questions.answer: A traveler.

questions.question: What was special about this traveler’s heart and mind?
questions.answer: He was passionate and full of questions.

questions.question: What had he been trying to find?
questions.answer: The Creator of the world.

questions.question: Before speaking directly, what kind of knowledge did he have?
questions.answer: Knowledge of Allah through signs.

questions.question: How many degrees of learning had he completed?
questions.answer: Eighteen.

questions.question: What happened when he reached the station of truth?
questions.answer: He came to direct address before Allah.

questions.question: To whom did he first explain this change?
questions.answer: To his own spirit.

questions.question: In the passage, what does the opening part of Surah al-Fatihah mainly contain?
questions.answer: Praise.

questions.question: What makes the word “iyyaka” important in the explanation?
questions.answer: It turns the speech into direct address.

questions.question: What should a seeker do instead of staying with only indirect clues?
questions.answer: Ask Allah directly.

questions.question: What example from creation is used to explain this better?
questions.answer: The example of the sun.

questions.question: How do people notice the sun in that example?
questions.answer: Through its rays.

questions.question: In a similar way, through what can people try to know Allah?
questions.answer: Through His Beautiful Names and sacred attributes.
